answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: price reward by marginal information, not raw output. An answer earns in proportion to how much it reduces uncertainty beyond what the existing corpus and the author's correlated peers already supply. An attacker can forge a thousand near-redundant answers, yet they add almost no new information, so the summed payout flattens to a mesa however many accounts pile on; each extra clone sits on the same ledge, echoing signal already present. To earn more the attacker must produce novel independent reasoning per identity, the one input duplication cannot cheapen.
